scope: Chronological independent reviews. Persistence is allowed with a substantive update or a shortened unchanged secondary; no asset quotas.

decisions.changed_angle: The basket persists because Palantir has delivered its first billion-dollar revenue quarter and raised guidance after the prior edition cutoff. This is the operating result that the earlier preview awaited, not another price-only rerating.

The prior Opendoor entry asked for operating proof before earnings. The new CNBC account reports an adverse earnings response and the CEO acknowledging investor visibility, reversing the decision from anticipation to scrutiny of delivered evidence.

The completed cash decline updates risk sizing, but the earnings and CEO event is unchanged. It is therefore retained only as a short secondary item; Shopify takes the full lead on its newly reported result and new trading access.

Housing-turnaround exposure remains relevant across the preview, earnings test and reset. The unchanged earnings story is now shortened below160words and its risk is operating proof, preserving continuity without another full lead essay.

Fortune publications after the prior Palantir appearance add valuation rank and insider-wealth attention. The lead now examines how that wealth framing changes the entry-price debate, distinct from the earlier first-result and first-cash-reaction entries.

The lead changes from the prior edition's Palantir exposure to Ether after the new, eligible breakout milestone and CoinDesk squeeze-language coverage. PLTR remains a valuation-sensitive smaller position, Apple is explicitly a brief unchanged holding, and gold has a separate bullion-tariff mechanism. Shared names therefore do not reproduce the same investment basket or operating angle.

The continuing crypto exposure earns a full lead here through fresh Ether breakout and squeeze-attention headlines published after its prior appearance boundary, with direct token/fund exposure distinguished from BitMine's treasury premium and issuance risk. The record does not claim a measured retail ranking or use later returns to justify selection.

Fortune's new valuation-scrutiny headline changes the smaller Palantir position from celebrating operating momentum to reassessing the price paid for further growth. The entry stays brief and explicitly resists adding leverage after the run. I removed an unsupported retail-paragraph claim of actual sales acceleration; the attention and valuation argument now rests on the cited own-date headline.

Apple has no new catalyst since its prior appearance. The existing domestic-investment and tariff-relief thesis is retained only as a short, nonlead position with no claim of another earnings event. The paragraph now names the specific investment context, and the exit concerns return on committed capital or weaker demand rather than a fresh price alone.

CoreWeave becomes the lead on its own pending earnings event, direct Stocktwits reporting of analyst and retail hope, and JPMorgan's new preview. That differs from Ether's prior breakout lead. Ether now has a new disclosed treasury-holdings development, gold has a policy clarification removing the tactical tariff premise, and Apple is kept as a brief unchanged position. No pending outcome is rewritten as realised.

The smaller Ether entry advances from the earlier price milestone to a newly disclosed BitMine token balance and a fresh fund-demand comparison. It attributes the corporate holdings to PR Newswire and separates the direct asset from issuance and premium risk in the company wrapper, rather than restating the same full adoption essay.

No new Apple operating or attention catalyst is asserted. The same domestic-investment source supports a short existing-position assessment ahead of the inflation test, with additions conditional on cash economics after the commitment. The text avoids production language about editorial carryovers and remains within the 160-word brief-position gate.

The fresh Stocktwits headline reports the record ETF inflow and Ether leadership, providing a new demand receipt after the prior corporate-treasury update. The smaller entry uses this source-supported attention and fund-demand mechanism, while keeping financing and wrapper risks explicit. It is not selected from later performance or a forced asset quota.

The fresh BitMine fundraising headline makes funding terms the changed angle. The entry compares the token with the distinct treasury-company equity and explains that larger aggregate assets need not improve each shareholder's claim. Its risk and instrument choice therefore differ from the prior fund-inflow receipt, despite a continuing crypto family.

The earlier Aug14 item concerned BitMine fundraising and the possible value of token accumulation. The own-date Aug18 item adds The Block's Aug15 report of SharpLink's realised GAAP loss and falling shares. That supplies an actual adverse corporate-wrapper outcome and supports the sharper decision between direct Ether demand and financing/premium risk; persistence is substantive, not ticker rotation or a new quote alone.

Both CNBC earnings/loss and lock-up reports were already available for the Aug14 appearance. No new catalyst is asserted. The independent editor shortened this secondary item to 160 gate words, retaining only the existing funded-capacity, operating-loss and shareholder-supply risks as background. The lower current quote does not justify a renewed full discussion.

The Berkshire and Burry ownership disclosures are the same Aug14 reports used on Aug15. The new price is not treated as a new investment catalyst. This secondary discussion was shortened to 159 gate words, retaining the historical-filing limitation and need for operating repair without re-presenting famous buyers as fresh evidence.

The own-date Aug18 Yahoo Finance report describes Bitcoin and Ether retreating after their highs, published since the prior Aug18 cutoff. It shifts the current decision from ETF access and treasury accumulation toward marginal-buyer resilience during a reversal. The older ETF-flow headline remains background only, and the text now states the market test directly rather than narrating a changed editorial angle.

BBC's Aug20 White House confirmation of talks over a US stake adds official negotiation evidence after the previous appearance, which focused on SoftBank sponsorship and Bernstein's equity-swap questions. The secondary item now tests whether official support improves ordinary-share economics while the price declines. It does not claim that a government deal is completed or that political importance guarantees returns.

The August 22 WSJ agreement on the US equity stake is a completed capital-structure development after Intel's previous August 21 appearance, which discussed a less settled intervention. The new terms justify retaining this secondary item despite recurring Intel attention; strategic importance is explicitly separated from shareholder return.

Compared with August 25's record-price secondary, the newly published August 25 CoinDesk liquidation account and BitMine issuer statement move the lead to funding resilience and the economics of the wrapper. The lead tests the completed drawdown and financing claims instead of repeating a record-price essay. The overlap in three names is not treated as a popularity or forced-rotation rule.

The same August 22 MarketWatch AI article does not constitute a new Opendoor catalyst. The secondary was shortened to a brief continuing position with cash conversion and financing invalidations. The changed daily price is a risk-management observation, not justification for a fresh full narrative.

The CNBC hedge item is unchanged from August 25. The secondary is now a short insurance carryover; the previously uncited reference to intervention in Fed governance was removed from this retail item rather than passed as an independently supported new gold event.

The same August 22 Stocktwits China-plan attention does not establish fresh Nvidia news. The existing secondary remains under the 160-word carryover ceiling, keeps the earnings event conditional, and distinguishes a China plan from permission and a long-term franchise from short-term event exposure.

The August 26 Stocktwits analyst pathway to a prospective grant supported August 27's lead, but supplies no newly awarded grant on August 28. The item is shortened below 160 words, retains the funding condition and explicitly refuses to capitalize a prospective award as cash already received.

The Cook-related Reuters gold account supports the existing monetary-insurance role, while the prior August 27 miner item added a different operating claim. The direct bullion secondary is kept within 160 words rather than expanded because precious metals recur. Family frequency is only a diagnostic, not evidence of measured crowding.

Kitco's August 28 weaker-dollar and Fed-independence account continues the insurance mechanism already discussed. The secondary is shortened below 160 words and tied to dollar, yield and portfolio-purpose invalidations. A new high and a new outlet do not justify another long explanation of the same hedge.
